source_name: K-Monitor Adatbázis (transparency NGO press + procurement database)
why_relevant: Curated, tagged index of Hungarian media reporting on public procurement and public spending, plus a network database of companies and owners. Excellent pointer layer for finding contested/large ATM, cash-logistics and payment-IT contracts and the corporate actors behind them, which then leads back to the primary notices.

source_name: khf.hu – Közbeszerzési Hirdetmény Figyelő (commercial notice-monitoring service)
why_relevant: Commercial monitoring service that aggregates Hungarian procurement notices with keyword alerting. Useful as a redundancy/alerting channel for ATM, POS, kártya and készpénzszállítás keywords in case direct EKR/Értesítő crawling breaks.

source_name: TenderHelp Hungary – EKR/TED guidance and tender interface explainer
why_relevant: Practitioner-oriented explainer of the Hungarian tendering interfaces (EKR, TED, KEF, DKÜ) — useful for correctly modelling which portal carries which class of notice, and for glossary/terminology building.

source_name: BKK Zrt. – jegy- és bérletautomata beszerzés / üzemeltetés announcements
why_relevant: Budapest transport authority ran a procurement to renew and operate its ticket-vending machine network, with new contract expected 2025 and devices from 2026. TVMs are card-accepting payment endpoints: the notices and BKK's own communications disclose machine counts, card-payment share (>70% of automat purchases) and cashless-only device counts — a rare quantified cash-vs-card dataset outside banking.

source_name: MÁV-csoport – jegykiadó automata telepítés és beszerzés
why_relevant: State railway group installing 110 new ticket machines (93 at bus stations, 11 HÉV, 6 rail; 30 card-only). Procurement and maintenance notices for these machines (incl. earlier JKA1/JKA2/JKA3 L3-level maintenance of 170 units seen in the Értesítő) quantify unattended card-acceptance fleet size and service vendors.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár / Jogtár – ATM installation law 2025. évi XVIII. tv. and 19/2025 (VI.26.) MNB rendelet
why_relevant: The 2025 ATM-installation law and the MNB decree on siting criteria and cost-sharing between payment service providers create a legally mandated ATM roll-out (every settlement ≥1,000 residents by end-2025) and joint installation/operation contracts due by 31 July 2025. This is the demand driver behind the ATM procurement/tender wave and defines who must contract with whom — essential context for interpreting notices.

source_name: TED CPV vocabulary reference (Common Procurement Vocabulary)
why_relevant: Authoritative CPV code list needed to build the deterministic query set for ATM (cash dispensers), payment terminals, card production/personalisation, security/cash-in-transit and financial-IT services in both TED and the Hungarian database (which also supports obsolete codes).

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Adatbázisok hub (registries: contracts, authorities, sanctions, arbitration)
why_relevant: Hub page listing all statutory registries maintained by the Public Procurement Authority (contract database, contracting-authority register, Döntőbizottság decisions, etc.). The gateway for discovering secondary datasets that reveal contract modifications and disputes on ATM/POS/cash contracts.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – archív hirdetményminták (notice templates archive)
why_relevant: Official notice templates (incl. result notices for framework-agreement based procurements) define the field structure of Hungarian notices — needed to build reliable parsers that extract quantities, values and winners from historical notices.

source_name: Tietoevry Banking newsroom / press releases (card platform customer wins)
why_relevant: Tietoevry publicly announced completion of OTP Bank Hungary's card acquiring software replacement (Card Suite). Vendor newsroom is a recurring channel for HU card-processing migrations, scope and go-live dates that private banks never publish themselves.

source_name: ACI Worldwide investor news releases (Hungary real-time payments customers)
why_relevant: ACI has published named Hungarian deployments (OTP Bank Group, Erste Bank Hungary, Takarékinfo/Takarék Group, Budapest Bank, MKB) plus a claimed share of HU instant-payment traffic (~75%). Rare quantified indirect indicator of who runs which payment rails.

source_name: Capsys Informatikai Kft. — news / references
why_relevant: Named ACI implementation partner for Hungary's instant payment go-live; a domestic integrator whose own news page is likely to name additional HU bank clients not visible on the international vendor side.

source_name: Laurel Számítástechnikai Kft. — Referenciák (client reference page)
why_relevant: Hungarian financial-sector software house with an explicit customer-reference page; Laurel is also reported as co-developer with Raiffeisen Bank on an MNB-supported electronic payment solution. Reference lists are the classic indirect route to private-bank supplier relationships.

source_name: CARDNET Zrt. (Hungarian POS terminal / payment terminal service provider)
why_relevant: Domestic supplier of payment-terminal software, terminal management and transaction services to Hungarian financial institutions; installs terminals on behalf of banks. A prime indirect source for POS estate structure and bank-vendor mapping.

source_name: Euronet ATM Magyarország (euronetatms.com HU site)
why_relevant: Independent ATM deployer operating a large HU estate and providing outsourced ATM services; its HU site plus Euronet Worldwide quarterly ATM counts give an independent read on ATM density and the non-bank share of the estate.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf banking case studies & press archive
why_relevant: Diebold has publicly announced HU deployments with unit counts (approx. 180 Opteva banknote-acceptor ATMs to UniCredit Bank Hungary Zrt., plus maintenance/professional services). Its CEE case studies routinely disclose fleet sizes, uptime SLAs and outsourcing scope.

source_name: ANY Biztonsági Nyomda Nyrt. (card manufacturing & personalisation supplier)
source_subtype: supplier corporate site + listed-issuer financial reports
why_relevant: Listed HU security printer producing VISA/Mastercard chip cards and performing card personalisation, PIN mailing and statement personalisation for banks and insurers. As a Budapest Stock Exchange issuer it also files annual/quarterly reports with segment revenue — an unusually quantitative indirect proxy for HU card issuance volumes.

source_name: bankkartya.hu — sajtószemle / kártyagyártók (card-industry press digest)
why_relevant: Hungarian card-industry news digest with a dedicated 'kártyagyártók' (card manufacturers) category — a local-language pointer into the HU card supplier ecosystem and bank-supplier relationships.

source_name: G4S Készpénzlogisztikai Kft. (HU cash-handling / CIT supplier)
why_relevant: Reported to run ATM replenishment for OTP and foreign-owned banks and cash processing for major retail chains; with MPT Security held ~85-90% of HU CIT market revenue. Supplier-side view of cash cycle volumes and bank outsourcing.

source_name: T-Systems Magyarország Zrt. — banking references / news
why_relevant: Named delivery partner for the instant payment system at Takarékinfo and co-partner on ACI's HU real-time payments rollout; a major HU bank IT integrator whose case studies and news reveal private-bank projects procured outside public portals.

source_name: 4iG Nyrt. / 4iG Informatikai Zrt. — solutions, references and BÉT disclosures
why_relevant: Leading HU IT/ICT group and listed issuer; system-integration supplier to financial institutions. Its solution/reference pages plus regulated disclosures can reveal bank infrastructure contracts that private banks do not announce.

source_name: hu.openprocurements.com — supplier-side procurement index (HU)
why_relevant: Aggregates HU public procurement by SUPPLIER and CPV code (e.g. 72230000 custom software development), letting one profile a vendor's public-sector wins and infer its banking-sector capability set even when the private-bank contracts themselves are invisible.

source_name: GVH sectoral inquiry report on the card acceptance market (2019)
why_relevant: Competition-authority sectoral inquiry that compelled data from eight banks, four non-bank card-acceptance providers and two card schemes — effectively a regulator-forced disclosure of the private acquiring/terminal supplier structure that vendors and banks otherwise keep private.

source_name: MNB rendelet 19/2025 + methodological guide on mandated ATM installation (bank-by-bank allocation)
why_relevant: The regulation enumerates which bank must install ATMs in which settlements (OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104 of 1,039 units), creating a rare bank-level, unit-level ATM pipeline. This is the demand signal that drives HU ATM vendor procurement over 2025-2026.

source_name: Bank360 / money.hu / szeretlekmagyarorszag ATM-allocation trackers
why_relevant: HU comparison/news sites republish the bank-by-settlement ATM allocation lists in machine-friendlier form and follow the rollout, giving a cheap tracking layer for who is actually deploying (and therefore who is buying ATMs).

source_name: Portfolio Financial IT conference programme (vendor-bank speaker pairings)
why_relevant: The annual HU Financial IT conference agenda pairs named bank executives with named vendors and sponsors; agendas and sponsor lists are a reliable annual snapshot of which suppliers are currently engaged with which Hungarian banks.

source_name: Mastercard / Visa Hungary press communications naming bank deployments
why_relevant: Scheme-side HU communications name issuing/acquiring banks adopting specific capabilities (e.g. Decision Intelligence fraud scoring used by numerous HU financial institutions), giving a supplier-side read on card-technology adoption across private banks.
